request: how do I compute the Gini impurity on both sides of a split and the information gain?

composition.story: How much does this split improve purity? Compute each node's Gini: G = 1 − Σp², where p is its class proportion. Start with the parent, then inspect both children. Weight child impurities by sample fractions before subtracting from the parent. The final comparison shows Gini gain; entropy-based information gain uses entropy instead.

aha.observation: Weighting both children gives remaining impurity 0.250; subtracting it from the parent's 0.500 gives a Gini gain of 0.250.

parts.presentation: Use the approved card shell, with the story above the experiment. Keep step position and calculation progress on this rail.
Keep Parent, Left child, and Right child visible in fixed positions. Highlight only the active region. Letters represent equally weighted samples.
Anchor beside the active region without covering samples. Use the bound text as the status line; show its reason beneath.
Report numbers only here, beneath the picture. Gini is dimensionless, ranging from zero to one-half for these binary classes. Round results to three decimals.

controls.label: Calculation step
controls.presentation: Use Previous and Next with visible focus and keyboard operation. Default to parent; advance one state within parent through gain. Preserve disabled boundary names. Every state persists until another action. Brief parameter-control budget: zero, excluding navigation and reset.

controls.label: Reset
controls.presentation: Restore the parent state and all defaults. Support keyboard activation and visible focus. Reference captures must show gain before reset.

variants.label: Fixed binary split with unequal child sizes

states.label: Parent impurity
states.sentence: Calculate the Parent's impurity before evaluating the split.
states.why: Class proportions use this node's samples as the denominator.

states.label: Left child impurity
states.sentence: Calculate the Left child's impurity using only its own samples.
states.why: Every sample belongs to the same class, so this child is pure.

states.label: Right child impurity
states.sentence: Calculate the Right child's impurity using its own class proportions.
states.why: This child contains both classes, so its impurity remains positive.

states.label: Weighted impurity and gain
states.sentence: Subtract the sample-weighted child impurity from the Parent's impurity.
states.why: The larger Right child contributes more; an unweighted average would misrepresent the split.

readouts.label: Gini gain = Parent Gini − weighted child Gini
